decisions.reason: Step 1.1 omitted the direct Borel-to-Lebesgue inclusion citation, although that theorem already lies behind the interval-measure supplier. Added F10 and its direct dependency, with Countable Choice explicit. Relative Borel preimages are Borel in R since [0,1] is closed; boundedness on measure-one [0,1] gives integrability. Both integrals are within epsilon of the same finite left sum, proving equality without changing the Statement.

The tableau coefficients were defined correctly, but the IVP formulas left t,u,h implicit despite the cited RK definition requiring (t,u) in D, h>0, and admissible stage points. Stated those domains explicitly. Cardinal integration still gives u_h(c_i)=U_i, u_h prime(c_i)=hF_i and the endpoint identity; no branch solvability is asserted. All direct consumers use the same forward-step/admissible-stage convention or only the unchanged coefficient integrals.

The invariance-certified exit was not determined by the enumerated inputs. Added a caller-supplied Boolean invariance_certified with the exact quantified inner-map guarantee as the admissibility condition for true, and made step 2 read it explicitly. False returns contraction-not-certified. The guarantee is established externally; no undecidable universal test is hidden in the procedure. Strict lower triangularity still determines each new stage, the initial columns cancel, K=0 performs only predictor calls, and acceptance still returns U^k with cached endpoint values. Direct consumer formulas and all stage-call counts remain unchanged.

The negative-step algebraic counterexample is outside the actual collocation-stage interface: def-collocation-quadrature-tableau invokes the implicit Runge-Kutta equations of def-implicit-runge-kutta-stage-equations, whose Definition explicitly fixes h>0. That restriction already applied before the tableau clarification; negative-h algebraic roots are not admissible collocation branches here. With inherited h>0, subtraction gives d_stage<=d_start+hL norm(Q)d_stage, hence the factor 2, and endpoint subtraction gives 1+2hL norm(b). The original item bytes are restored; no mathematical carrier repair is needed.

The original step 3.1 applied the global-error theorem without proving numerical endpoint containment in its tube. Preserved the order-two claim and made exact initialization explicit. Added a uniform compact convex neighborhood within the C2 domain, local midpoint stage balls with h B_+/2<=r and h L_+/2<=1/2, and a prefix error bootstrap. Stability and O(h^3) exact-start defect yield e_{n+1}<=(1+2L_+h)e_n+Ch^3; the discrete recurrence bounds e_n<=C_T h^2<r on every prefix, so every step exists and all stages and endpoints remain in the enlarged tube. Uniqueness by stage subtraction identifies this local solution with the assumed branch. No numerical-tube premise was added to bypass the gap. Final bootstrap phase is numbered 4.1 as required by precheck. Reexamined the unchanged mathematical effect of restoring the stability supplier: its inherited h>0 premise and the bound used here still hold. The <=1/2 condition is exactly the smallness premise needed for the factor-2 stability supplier.

The old title claimed an exact IVP solution, although a two-node collocation polynomial has degree at most two while the exact path is t^4/4. Renamed the title to assert the exact one-step endpoint. The proof correctly matches Gaussian and collocation cardinal weights by integral agreement and integrates the cubic field exactly, giving sum b_j c_j^3=1/4. The state-independent stage equations are finite and unique. No Statement or Definition changed.

The collocation polynomial u_h is the object defined through def-collocation-quadrature-tableau and def-implicit-runge-kutta-stage-equations; the latter already requires h>0. The scaled-derivative supplier also fixes its asymptotic branch as h decreases to zero from above in A1. Thus sufficiently small h<=h0 in this forward-step interface excludes negative h, and the odd-power norm bound is well signed. Checked the full weighted proof: P prime=-PB and e prime=Be-r give e(1)=h integral P(g-I_M g); P-q=O(h^M), interpolation error O(h^M), and Gauss Hermite remainder for qg yield the claimed O(h^(2M+1)). The original item bytes are restored; no edit is warranted.

F3 misreported a guaranteed O(h) error bound as an upper limit on possible order. Corrected F3 and its use in step 2.1. Independently, the invariant stage ball [0,2u], q=h/2, exact initialization and exp bounds ensure the first residual check returns U0 and hence Euler endpoints (1+h)^n. Comparing binomial and exponential coefficients gives e-(1+1/N)^N>=1/(2N), so this actual example is not order two regardless of the generic theorem guarantee. The accepted residual is also >=h/2 and fails the h^3 target. Statement and Example are unchanged. Explicitly supplied the new true invariance flag; the already proved [0,2u] self-map inequality is its exact guarantee.

The bare tableau did not specify an SDC preconditioner, so the Q_Delta=0 assertion lacked its actual algorithm prerequisite. Declared and cited the explicit-left-Euler sweep and specified that choice in Given, F5 and step 1.1. Its one-node strictly lower triangular block is zero and S(V)=1-(h/2)V, making S(V)-V=-G(V). The independent implicit-stage proof remains valid: [0,2] maps into [0.9,1], q=1/20, U*=20/21, |G(V)|=21/40000, and residual/(1-q)=21/38000<h^3. Endpoint error h/2000=1/20000<h^4 is a single-step estimate, with no global conclusion. No Statement or Definition changed.
